title: Redwood structured output + function calling demo - Orion Analytics
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Orion Analytics through structured output (JSON mode), schema enforcement, and function/tool calling. Demo included Console walkthrough and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. Customer asked about data residency, SOC2/KMS, and hosted vs Dedicated latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: provide pricing/security pack, run a short POC with schema and baseline benchmarks, and schedule a tech deep dive for private deployment.
next_steps: Maya to send tailored pricing and SOC2/security pack (incl. KMS & audit log docs)
Liam to set up POC baseline: 2 endpoints, sample dataset, and perf script - target week of 2027-06-28
Customer to share 3 representative schema examples and sample prompts
Schedule Private deployment deep dive (SE-led) after POC results
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pricing, SOC2 pack, and reference deck - due 2027-06-22
Liam O'Neill: Provision POC infra and share runbook + perf script - due 2027-06-25
Carlos Reyes: Share sample schemas and 200 example prompts - due 2027-06-24
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Carlos Reyes (Orion), Priya Nair (Orion), Dana Kurt (Orion)

Summary (auto): quick demo of JSON structured-output + function calling, console tour, Optimize suggestions, questions about security and deployment options.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Maya here from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we've got liam from the SE team who will lead the demo.
00:22 Carlos Reyes: hey thanks, super excited, we had a quick pre-read, but want to see how JSON mode could help our ingestion pipeline.
00:36 Liam O'Neill: great, i will share my screen, um starting with the API quickstart, then switch to console and show structured output and function calling. bear with me if the screen flickers.
01:10 Liam O'Neill: so first, JSON mode — we set a schema in the request and the model returns a validated JSON object, or an enforcement failure. here i'm using a product-catalog example: fields like id, name, price, price_currency, attributes array. note the schema is strict but we can set tolerant parsing.
02:05 Priya Nair: quick Q — can the schema enforce types and enums? like we only want price_currency to be USD or EUR.
02:18 Liam O'Neill: yeah absolutely, you can declare enums and types. if the model outputs something off-schema we have three choices: auto-correct, reject and return a structured error, or return best-effort with a warning. those are guardrail policies you can set per-route.
03:00 Dana Kurt: and that lives at the API level or console? we want this enforced across all teams.
03:12 Liam O'Neill: both; you can define schema templates in the console and pin them to routes, or embed per-request. enterprise customers often centralize templates in the private control plane.
03:38 Maya Chen: quick aside: we'll attach the sample schema deck after the call — link in the notes: https://redwood.dev/decks/schemas-demo (note: demo asset).
04:05 Carlos Reyes: how about function calling? we have downstream systems that need strictly typed webhook payloads.
04:22 Liam O'Neill: demo time — i'm going to show tool/function calling. here the model recognizes an intent and returns a function invocation like {"tool":"create_product","args":{...}} which we map to your service. you can validate the args against a JSON schema before executing the tool.
05:05 Liam O'Neill: watch this — model suggests calling create_product with payload, console shows the invocation, we can set auto-execute or require manual approval.
05:40 Priya Nair: nice — manual approval could be helpful for high-risk operations. can we audit who executed which calls?
05:55 Liam O'Neill: yes, audit logs capture the user, route, model, generated payload, and whether the invocation was auto-run or approved. logs are exportable to S3 or forwarded to your SIEM.
06:25 Carlos Reyes: any limits on tool integration? e.g., can we integrate a Jenkins job or internal ETL?
06:38 Liam O'Neill: any HTTP-based webhook or internal tool is fine; we provide connectors and you can write custom adapters. we demoed a Postgres write adapter in the docs.
07:10 Dana Kurt: switching to performance — what's the latency hit when using structured output or function calling vs freeform text?
07:25 Liam O'Neill: minimal, usually a few ms for schema validation; main costs come from model selection and sequence length. we showed benchmarks in the perf spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.dev/benchmarks/json-mode). for high-throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity with pinned model variants.
08:05 Maya Chen: circling back to Optimize — liam, can you show batching and quantization suggestions?
08:20 Liam O'Neill: sure. Optimize analyzes token distributions and suggests batch sizes, cache TTLs for prefix caching, and quantization profiles per model. here it suggests int8 for our embedding-ish workload and continuous batching of 8-16 to hit cost targets without blowing latency SLOs.
09:05 Priya Nair: are these automated recommendations or do you apply them for us?
09:18 Liam O'Neill: currently they are recommendations you can apply in the console; for Dedicated customers we can help run tuning and apply safe rollouts.
09:40 Carlos Reyes: what about hallucinations or schema drift over time? we worry models slowly produce invalid payloads.
09:55 Liam O'Neill: we have monitoring + regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. if schema violations spike we alert and can auto-fallback to a conservative model or to rule-based templates.
10:30 Dana Kurt: security: we need SOC2, SSO, SAML, KMS support and control plane isolation.
10:45 Maya Chen: Redwood supports SOC2+, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations for envelope encryption. for Private deployments we can offer a customer-managed control plane and VPC peering or on-prem. we'll attach the security pack.
11:20 Priya Nair: data residency: can logs be limited to EU?
11:30 Liam O'Neill: yes — region pinning plus log routing. for Dedicated/Private you can keep logs in your region or export to your cloud.
12:00 Carlos Reyes: cost — how do we estimate per-call unit economics with structured output?
12:15 Liam O'Neill: cost depends on token count plus any added routing/transform steps, but structured output often reduces downstream parsing costs. Optimize can simulate estimated cost reductions with batching/caching applied.
13:05 Maya Chen: ok demo move — i'm going to show a Console route setup: route -> schema template -> model variant -> fallback policy -> RBAC.
13:25 Liam O'Neill: notice we added a canary rollout and a model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized model under load.
14:10 Priya Nair: do you support canary by customer segment? we need per-tenant routing.
14:22 Liam O'Neill: yes, routing rules support headers, org-id, or any attribute. you can route premium customers to Dedicated pools and others to hosted.
15:00 Dana Kurt: about the POC, what do you need from us?
15:12 Maya Chen: sample schemas, representative prompt set, basic traffic profile, and success criteria (latency, throughput, error tolerance). we'll run a 2-week POC.
15:40 Carlos Reyes: sounds good. regarding private deploy, we may need on-prem for some regs, ideally an air-gapped option.
15:52 Liam O'Neill: we do an on-prem package for regulated workloads; that includes audit logs, KMS integration with HSM connectors, and an agent for model serving. we'll plan a deep-dive on architecture if you want.
16:30 Priya Nair: curious — any gotchas with quantized models and function calling? we saw issues with argument truncation before.
16:45 Liam O'Neill: good point — quantization can slightly change tokenization boundaries; Redwood's runtime manages KV cache and tokenization to avoid argument truncation, but we recommend running sample prompts in the POC to validate edge cases.
17:20 Dana Kurt: will the generated function payload always be deterministic? we need idempotency.
17:32 Liam O'Neill: not fully deterministic by default; you can request deterministic decoding parameters and strict schema enforcement to drive deterministic outputs. also we recommend including request-level trace ids and checksums for idempotency.
18:05 Carlos Reyes: what about throttling and quotas for tool calls to our internal services?
18:20 Liam O'Neill: Redwood supports per-route rate limits and token quotas; plus a circuit-breaker on tool invocations so we can stop calling your service if error rates climb.
19:00 Maya Chen: quick note — i'll share a POC template and runbook after the call.
19:12 Liam O'Neill: switching back to the demo — here's a live JSON-mode run: prompt -> schema returned ok -> function invocation emitted -> validated -> auto-executed (we had auto-exec on this demo). you may see a small correction where the model spelled an attribute slightly off — that's expected in noisy transcriptions, but the schema fixed it.
20:05 Priya Nair: small nit — can we map model fields to our internal field names automatically?
20:18 Liam O'Neill: yes, transformation rules in the console can remap keys and run lightweight reformatters (e.g., date formats).
21:00 Dana Kurt: show us metrics: where do we see success in the Console?
21:12 Liam O'Neill: per-route dashboards show token breakdowns, latency histograms, function-calling rates, and cost per 1k tokens. you can break down by model-variant and tenant.
22:00 Carlos Reyes: do you store raw model outputs? we need to know for compliance.
22:12 Maya Chen: by default we store traces for X days (configurable), and you can disable storing raw outputs for sensitive routes; we store traces in your S3 if you prefer.
23:00 Priya Nair: can we self-host only the runtime but keep control plane with Redwood?
23:15 Liam O'Neill: yes — hybrid is supported: customer-managed runtime with Redwood control plane, or fully private.
24:00 Dana Kurt: handoff question — how do we validate schema correctness at scale? manual tests are tedious.
24:20 Liam O'Neill: we recommend unit test harnesses with our eval SDK; you can run nightly evals against sample prompt sets and get regression alerts.
25:00 Carlos Reyes: objections from procurement: price and long term vendor lock in.
25:20 Maya Chen: pricing: hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable commit; Private is license + support. we can provide migration guardrails and exportable data to reduce lock-in risk.
26:00 Priya Nair: any competitor differentiators?
26:12 Maya Chen: many vendors focus only on model access, we emphasize serving, cost controls, and production ops: rollouts, caching, and Optimize to keep unit economics stable.
27:00 Liam O'Neill: quick demo note — here's a function calling failure: invalid enum triggered reject policy; console displayed the error and suggested corrective patch to schema.
27:40 Dana Kurt: good. if we automate remediation, can we run a safe patch?
27:55 Liam O'Neill: safe patches can be staged as suggestions, but auto-patching is opt-in and should be accompanied by regression evals.
28:30 Carlos Reyes: timeline — if POC in july, and results look good, we may target q4 for production.
28:45 Maya Chen: sounds realistic. we'll scope the POC now and align stakeholders.
29:15 Priya Nair: legal/security will want the SOC2 and KMS details.
29:30 Maya Chen: will include in the pack.
30:00 Liam O'Neill: wrapping up with one more demo: Optimize suggestion that shows cost benefit of batching 12 requests vs no batching — you can see a projected 40% cost delta with minor p50 latency increase.
30:45 Dana Kurt: can Optimize simulate Dedicated savings with reserved capacity numbers?
30:55 Liam O'Neill: yes, it can run what-if scenarios assuming reserved commit levels.
31:30 Carlos Reyes: closing Q on function-calling security: are the tool payloads encrypted in transit to our webhooks?
31:42 Liam O'Neill: yes TLS mutual auth is supported; we also support signed webhook payloads for verification.
32:10 Maya Chen: recap and next steps: we'll send pricing/SOC2 pack, Liam will provision POC infra, customer will share schemas and prompts, schedule private deep dive.
32:40 Carlos Reyes: thanks all, looks good. we'll sync internally and set dates.

End of recording
